plus.analyst_notes:
Closes https://github.com/vz-risk/VCDB/issues/24645
Partner_Breach tag: coded from the partner's perspective per the project rule. Primary victim InvoiceCloud (the billing/payment platform whose access key was compromised); the City of Oshkosh utility and AquaHawk Alerting (the other billing platform involved) are secondary victims. The incident_id reuses 2D848031-3327-46AF-951C-97FC03FAC81B from the row already in Partner_Breaches_2027_dbir.csv so the two stay linked.
Template Hacking-ext-unknown used, refined to Use of stolen creds because InvoiceCloud 'disabled the compromised access key' (an API/access key). Vector Partner: the access ran through the vendor integration; which party's key was compromised, and how, is not stated. The CSV row coded variety Unknown; this record is more specific.
Data: names, emails, utility account numbers, invoice numbers (Personal). Number of customers not given.
Timeline: city notice dated October 9, 2026; when access began is not stated, so year 2026 only. dbir_year 2027.
Discovery: not stated, so Unknown.
Victim: InvoiceCloud (Braintree, Massachusetts), NAICS 522320 to match the CSV; employee count approximate. City of Oshkosh utility NAICS 221310 (the issue body said 2211, but the city utility bills water/sewer/storm water; change if needed).
Single source; confidence Medium.

event_chain.summary: Compromised access key used to read utility customer account data

summary: The City of Oshkosh, Wisconsin notified select utility customers by email on October 9, 2026 that unauthorized users had accessed their account details through the city's third-party billing vendors, InvoiceCloud and AquaHawk. Exposed data included customer names, email addresses, utility account numbers and invoice numbers; Social Security, driver's license and state ID numbers, banking and card data and passwords were not exposed. InvoiceCloud immediately disabled the compromised access key.
